fixes.explanation: That's it, baker! Here's the verse: "For the LORD has chosen Jacob as His own, Israel as His treasured possession." (Psalm 135:4) The psalm calls Israel treasured, not tolerated, not put up with. TREASURED. That's the kind of word you'd want said about you.

That's right! The psalm says, "The idols of the nations are silver and gold, made by the hands of men." (Psalm 135:15) People made them. Imagine a thing that needs YOU to make it, and then can't even speak.

Eli was a priest (1 Samuel 1:9), so I see the thinking, friend. But the psalm doesn't call his house here. It says, "O house of Israel, bless the LORD; O house of Aaron, bless the LORD…" (Psalm 135:19) Aaron is the name it uses.
Yes, Jerusalem! The psalm says, "Blessed be the LORD from Zion—He who dwells in Jerusalem." (Psalm 135:21) That's the last blessing before the closing Hallelujah. That's a good ending.

Bethel is a place Jacob named (Genesis 28:19), friend, but it's not in this verse. The psalm says, "Blessed be the LORD from Zion—He who dwells in Jerusalem." (Psalm 135:21) Jerusalem is the one named.
Hebron is where Sarah died (Genesis 23:2), friend, but this psalm doesn't name it. It says, "Blessed be the LORD from Zion—He who dwells in Jerusalem." (Psalm 135:21) Jerusalem is the answer.
